newsitem.title: UK: UK sets up group to review British film industry.
newsitem.headline: UK sets up group to review British film industry.

text.p: UK films minister Tom Clarke on Wednesday said a film policy review group has been set up to look at ways of boosting the film industry and cinema attendance in Britain.
The objective of the group -- to be co-chaired by Clarke and Stewart Till, an executive of PolyGram NV's Filmed Entertainments' unit -- is to produce an "action plan" by early next year.
"The new government is serious about the film industry," Clarke said in a statement, adding the government wanted to double the audience for British films.

"Our aim is to produce an achievable agenda for action for the industry and Government support to it. Stewart Till and I are delighted to be working with a group of leading lights from all the key sectors of film".

The group will be made up of "a blend of established big-hitters and the new generation of innovative film makers", whose credits include 'Four Weddings and a Funeral', 'The Commitments' and 'The Madness of King George'.
